items.title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users
items.summary: An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, an open-source inference engine, and ran code on one of NEAR AI's inference servers last Sunday. The attacker could also have seen requests being processed on that server that day, including requests sent in confidenti
items.content:
An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang , an open-source inference engine, and ran code on one of NEAR AI's inference servers last Sunday.

The attacker could also have seen requests being processed on that server that day, including requests sent in confidential mode, the company said earlier this week. That mode processes requests inside a trusted execution environment (TEE) designed to keep them private even from the company itself.

But the TEE "does not protect against a vulnerability in the software running inside the environment," the company said. SGLang runs inside the TEE, which is how the attacker could reach requests there.

That access has since been closed, but not before the attacker moved further into the company's systems.

The attacker reached an internal system behind Private Chat, a product the company had already deprecated. So far, the company has confirmed that the attacker downloaded account details for about 100 users there. These are email addresses and names, and for some accounts, plan and balance information.

The company found no sign that stored Private Chat conversations or uploaded files were accessed.

The attacker also reached 18 AI agents on an older deployment of NEAR AI Agents that did not run inside the company's TEE. From those agents, the attacker took data including chat history, settings and logs.

Two customers' NEAR AI Cloud API keys were exposed in logs. The company has revoked both.

After detecting the attack, the company revoked all active sessions and administrator credentials, replaced all agent tokens and took Private Chat offline. It also deployed a fix for the SGLang flaw on all of its inference servers, rotated its remaining credentials and completed a full forensic review, according to its incident report .

Access to its NEAR AI Cloud service has been restored. The company reported the flaw to the SGLang project. It has not identified the flaw by CVE number, named the affected SGLang versions, or said whether the project has released a fix.

The company has contacted users whose account details or agents it confirmed were accessed. Affected users heard directly from security@near.ai, with the steps that apply to them. As a precaution, the company asks users to be careful with messages about their account or balance that they did not ask for.

In a follow-up post yesterday, it said users who have not heard from it do not need to do anything. It has not said whether people whose requests passed through the affected server last Sunday were among those contacted.

In an October 15 technical write-up , Brave, the browser maker, said its Leo assistant runs chats with the GLM 5.3 Flash model inside a TEE operated by NEAR AI.

NEAR AI has not said whether the affected server handled any of those chats.

밤이 되면 대형 금융사 보안팀장 A씨는 남아서 일할 직원을 추린다. 자신은 남고, 당장 분석하거나 처리해야 할 문제에 관련된 팀원 몇 명만 남긴다. 모두를 계속 붙잡아둘 수는 없기 때문이다. 낮 동안 들어온 점검 요청과 보고 요구를 처리하고 나면, 밤에는 로그를 들여다보고 이상 징후를 확인해야 한다. 사고는 발생했지만 공격까지 끝난 것은 아니다. 추가 피해를 막아야 하고, 다른 시스템에도 문제가 없는지 살펴야 한다. 그 사이 팀원들은 다른 부서로 옮길 자리를 알아보고 있다.

A씨는 데일리시큐와 인터뷰에서 이렇게 말했다. 자신이 힘들다는 이야기보다 팀원들의 상황을 설명할 때 말이 길어졌다. 다들 버티기 어려워하니 필요한 사람만 남기는 식으로 운영하고 있다는 것이다. 지친 직원들에게 다시 일을 맡겨야 하는 팀장의 부담도 컸다.

“같은 월급을 받는데 차라리 다른 곳에서 마음 편하게 일하는 게 낫다고 생각하는 거죠.”

여러 보안팀원들이 보안 업무를 내려놓고 차라리 다른 부서나 일반 기업으로 가고 싶어 한다. 누군가는 영업 현장에서 일하는 방안까지 알아본다고 했다. 회사를 그만두지 않더라도 보안 업무에서는 벗어나고 싶다는 뜻이다. 공격을 막을 방법을 찾아야 할 팀장이 이제는 그 일을 할 사람들이 얼마나 더 남아 있을지를 걱정하고 있었다.

최근 금융권에서 해킹과 정보 유출 사고가 잇따르면서 금융사의 보안 책임을 강화해야 한다는 요구가 커지고 있다. 금융소비자의 정보와 자산을 보호해야 하는 금융사의 의무는 무겁다. 예방할 수 있었던 위험을 방치했는지, 필요한 조치를 하지 않았는지 철저하게 조사해야 한다.

그러나 사고 이후의 조치가 실제 보안 강화로 연결되고 있는지는 별도로 살펴야 한다. 재발 방지 과제는 쌓이는데 이를 수행할 인력과 시간은 부족하고, 판단 권한은 제한된 채 책임만 커지고 있다.

데일리시큐는 대형 금융사 보안팀장 A씨와 인터뷰를 바탕으로 사고 대응 현장의 어려움과 개선 과제를 살펴봤다. 취재원 보호를 위해 이름과 소속, 내부 조직을 특정할 수 있는 정보는 공개하지 않는다.

A씨는 사고 이후 보안팀에 주어진 점검 범위를 확대하고, 기존 시스템을 개선하고, 새로운 보안 체계를 마련해야 한다. 재발 방지 대책도 수십 개씩 생긴다고 했다.

어느 것 하나 필요 없다고 말하기 어려운 과제들이다. 문제는 그 일을 기존 직원들이 맡는다는 점이다. 사고 수습이 시작됐다고 평소 하던 보안 업무가 멈추는 것도 아니다. 관제와 취약점 점검, 신규 시스템 검토를 계속하면서 추가 과제를 처리해야 한다.

“다 필요한 일인 건 알아요. 그런데 그 일을 누가 담당할 것인지가 문제입니다.”

과제 목록에 담당자와 완료 기한을 적는다고 실행할 시간이 생기지는 않는다. 낮에 처리하지 못한 일은 밤으로 밀리고, 주중에 끝내지 못한 일은 주말로 넘어간다. 필요한 인력이 제때 보강되지 않으면 그 간격을 메우는 것은 기존 직원들의 시간이다.

A씨는 함께 일하는 직원들에게 미안할 때가 많다고 했다. 지쳐 있다는 것을 알면서도 다시 일을 요청해야 하기 때문이다. 그렇다고 당장 해야 할 분석과 대응을 미뤄둘 수도 없다. 고객 피해로 이어질 수 있다는 생각에 팀장은 남고, 필요한 직원 일부를 더 남긴다.

이런 상황이 반복되면 팀 안에서는 서로의 피로를 알면서도 일을 나눠야 한다. 팀장은 직원들을 보호하고 싶지만 해야 할 과제를 줄일 권한은 충분하지 않다. 직원들도 팀의 사정을 알기에 쉽게 일을 놓지 못한다. 그렇게 개인의 책임감이 인력 부족을 떠받치는 상태가 이어진다.

금융사가 재발 방지 대책을 실행하려면 과제를 승인하는 방식부터 바꿀 필요가 있다. 담당자와 기한뿐 아니라 필요한 인원, 외부 지원, 기존 업무의 조정 범위를 함께 결정해야 한다. 새로운 일을 맡길 때 어떤 업무를 줄이거나 미룰 것인지도 판단해야 한다.

장기 대응에는 교대 인력과 휴식 계획이 필요하다. 사고 대응을 지속하려면 분석하고 판단할 사람의 집중력부터 유지돼야 한다. 보안팀의 야근으로 대책이 이행되고 있다는 사실을 정상적인 운영의 증거로 받아들여서는 안 된다.

A씨가 가장 우려한 것은 숙련 인력의 이탈이었다. 그는 직원들이 다른 부서로 업무를 옮길 방법을 알아보고 있다는 설명을 반복하며 착찹해 했다.

그 배경에는 업무량과 함께 사고 이후의 책임 추궁이 있었다. 새로운 대책을 수행하면서도 다음 문제가 생기면 다시 자신들이 책임져야 한다는 불안이 커진다는 것이다.

“하루에도 얼마나 많은 공격을 막고 있는지는 아무도 관심이 없습니다. 그런데 한 번 사고가 나면 그동안 무엇을 했느냐는 질책을 듣게 됩니다.”

그는 그동안 보안 업무의 성과가 사고 한 번으로 모두 부정되는 것 같다고 호소했다.

사고가 발생하면 예방과 대응 과정에서 무엇이 부족했는지 철저히 살펴야 한다. 다만 사고가 났다는 이유만으로 보안 담당자들의 노력과 전문성까지 부정해서는 안 된다.실제로 어떤 위험을 발견했고, 어떤 조치를 했으며, 무엇을 놓쳤는지 구체적으로 확인해야 한다.

이 과정이 생략된 채 보안부서 전체가 질책의 대상이 되면 직원들은 업무를 계속 맡을 이유를 찾기 어려워진다. 다른 부서에서도 같은 처우를 받으며 일할 수 있다면, 더 큰 부담과 책임을 감수하면서 보안 업무에 남아야 할 이유가 무엇인지 고민하게 된다는 것이다.

숙련자가 자리를 옮기는 것은 정원 한 명이 줄어드는 데 그치지 않는다. 내부 시스템의 특성과 과거의 이상 징후, 부서별 업무 구조, 긴급 상황에서 필요한 협의 경로를 아는 사람이 빠지는 일이다. 채용을 통해 인원을 보충하더라도 그 경험까지 즉시 채워지지는 않는다.

A씨는 사고 대응 경험과 공격 분석 능력은 사람을 새로 뽑는다고 바로 생기는 것이 아니라고 강조했다. 현장을 경험한 사람들이 하나둘 보안 업무를 떠나면 다음 공격에 대응할 조직의 역량도 약해질 수 있다는 우려였다.

숙련 인력을 지키려면 격려와 함께 구체적인 조치가 따라야 한다. 장기 대응 인력의 업무를 조정하고 대체 인력을 투입해야 한다. 전문성을 쌓을 교육 시간과 경력 경로를 보장하고, 부담에 걸맞은 보상도 검토해야 한다.

무엇보다 자신이 어떤 기준으로 평가받고 책임지는지 예측할 수 있어야 한다. 통제할 수 없는 결정까지 책임져야 한다고 느끼는 조직에 숙련 인력이 오래 남기는 어렵다.

보안 인력이 더 필요하다는 설명에 돌아오는 질문도 A씨를 답답하게 했다. AI를 활용할 수 없는지, 자동화할 일은 없는지, 실력 있는 한 사람으로 해결할 수 없는지 묻는다는 것이다.

A씨는 AI와 자동화가 필요하다는 데 동의했다. 자신들도 활용을 추진하고 있다고 했다. 다만 도구를 도입하면 이를 구축하고 검증하고 운영할 사람이 필요하다는 설명이었다.

“AI를 활용한 시스템을 구축하는 것도 사람이 해야 하고, 제대로 작동하는지 검증하고 운영하는 것도 사람이 해야 합니다.”

취약점을 점검하는 일과 사고를 분석하는 일, 신규 시스템을 검토하는 일은 필요한 경험과 전문성이 다르다. 뛰어난 직원 한 사람이 있다고 모든 업무를 동시에 감당할 수 있는 것도 아니다.

인터뷰에서 A씨는 최근 공격 대응 상황을 “매일 전쟁”이라고 표현했다. 특정 IP를 차단한 뒤에도 다른 IP에서 접근이 계속된다고 했다. 하나의 대응을 마치는 동안 다른 지점의 이상 징후를 확인해야 한다는 설명이다.

다만 반복되고 빠른 공격을 모두 AI 공격으로 단정할 수는 없다. A씨 역시 같은 방식과 프로토콜로 공격이 이뤄질 때 AI인지 일반 자동화 도구인지, 사람이 수행한 것인지 구분하기 어렵다고 말했다. 이번 인터뷰만으로 개별 사고의 AI 사용 여부를 확정할 수는 없다.

현장에 필요한 것은 어떤 도구가 모든 문제를 해결해줄 것이라는 기대보다 실제 업무를 줄이는 설계다. 반복적인 로그 정리와 자료 취합을 줄여 분석 시간을 확보하고, 중요한 경보를 우선 검토할 수 있도록 해야 한다. 자동화를 도입한 뒤에도 운영과 검증에 얼마나 많은 일이 필요한지 확인해야 한다.

자동화는 보안 인력이 더 중요한 일에 집중하도록 돕는 수단이어야 한다. 이를 이유로 필요한 인력 확보를 계속 미룬다면 기존 업무에 도구 구축과 운영 부담까지 더해질 수 있다.

Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235 flaws, Outlook zero-day

Today is Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, with security updates addressing a record-breaking 1,235 flaws, including one actively exploited Microsoft Outlook zero-day vulnerability.

This Patch Tuesday addresses 66 "Critical" vulnerabilities, 48 of which are Remote Code Execution (RCE), 15 are Elevation of Privilege (EoP), and three are Use-After-Free in Microsoft Edge.

The approximate number of bugs in each vulnerability category is listed below:

536 Elevation of Privilege Vulnerabilities

27 Security Feature Bypass Vulnerabilities

296 Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities

157 Information Disclosure Vulnerabilities

142 Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Vulnerabilities

Of the 1,235 vulnerabilities, approximately 639 are categorized under Windows or Microsoft Windows products/components.

When BleepingComputer reports on Patch Tuesday security updates, we only count vulnerabilities released by Microsoft on Patch Tuesday itself.

Therefore, today's total excludes 108 flaws fixed earlier this month, including one Entra Device Registration, 82 Mariner, and 25 Microsoft Edge flaws.

November's Patch Tuesday comes after a record-breaking 1,411 flaws in the October updates as Microsoft continues to use AI to find and patch vulnerabilities.

To learn more about the non-security updates released today, you can review our dedicated articles on the Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates  and the  Microsoft Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update .

This month's Patch Tuesday fixes one zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook that was exploited in attacks.

Microsoft classifies a zero-day flaw as publicly disclosed or actively exploited when no official fix is available.

The actively exploited zero-day vulnerability addressed in the November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates is:

CVE-2026-124194 - Microsoft Outlook Spoofing Vulnerability

Microsoft patched a Microsoft Outlook Spoofing zero-day vulnerability that was actively exploited in attacks to steal NTLM account hashes.

"An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and convince a user to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook," warns Microsoft.

"Opening the file could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information that could be used to impersonate the user. Exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction."

This type of vulnerability is known as an NTLM credential disclosure flaw, where a malicious attachment, when opened, causes Windows to connect to an attacker-controlled network share.

When connecting, Windows may automatically attempt to authenticate to the remote server, exposing the user's NTLMv2 authentication hash, which can then be captured by the attacker and potentially cracked offline.

The recovered credentials could then be used to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts.

Similar vulnerability have been exploited in the past , typically through malicious attachments sent in phishing campaigns .

Other vendors who released updates or advisories in November 2026 include:

Barracuda Networks released security updates for two vulnerabilities that can let attackers run commands with root privileges. A week later, these flaws were exploited in attacks .

Cisco released security updates for numerous products, including critical vulnerabilities Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Secure Email Gateway, and Meraki.

Google released emergency security updates to patch a new Chrome vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks.

Ivanti released security updates to patch two Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway flaws that have been chained in zero-day attacks since at least October 1.

items.content:
David Turturean, a recent MIT graduate and a member of the technical staff at the startup lab Physical Superintelligence (PSI) , used early access to Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model to solve an 18-year-old problem about quantum computing.

“I’m totally accepting the idea that this might be the last paper I ever put out,” Turturean, who deferred plans to pursue a master’s at MIT’s prestigious computer science and AI lab to join PSI, told TechCrunch. “In a few months, like, why would you even put out a paper?”

The problem in question, the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, concerns the ability of quantum computers to solve problems faster than classical ones. Scott Aaronson, one of the two researchers who posed the problem, writes that he doesn’t quite understand the proof but that he believes it’s correct because it was autoformalized in Lean, a coding language for math, and explained by a team of top researchers with whom PSI shared the solution.

The solution appears to close the door on one avenue quantum computers could follow to solve certain difficult problems at high speed, but not all of them. “It’s a negative result that allows people to know, okay, we’re no longer looking there,” Turturean said.

More broadly, it reflects the upheaval in the scientific world caused by AI problem-solving.

“A proof of full [Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture] was one of the last remaining open problems in quantum query complexity that everyone seemed to agree was centrally important,” Aaronson, who described himself feeling satisfied, awestruck, disappointed, and fatigued by the news, wrote. “I was surprised, honestly, to see it missing from OpenAI’s Mathocalypse dump a few weeks ago. Surely they tried it, so was it really so much harder than all the problems that were solved?”

That’s a point in favor of PSI’s model, which is to solve scientific problems with specialized model harnesses and scaffolding.

“An effective kind of research system should have lots of things related to harnesses, lots related to tools, memory systems, simulation infrastructure,” PSI CEO Matt Pines told TechCrunch. “You want to be able to really go after a problem at breadth and depth, and be able to consider a wide range of potential alternatives.”

For now, the company’s revenue comes from using its tools to optimize data centers, simulating the variables of heat, power, water, sound — “where the performance of that site as well as its impact on the community are a direct function of its physics.” The long play, however, is converting theoretical physics breakthroughs into actual technologies.

“Six to nine months ago, when I was talking to investors, like I had to sort of stretch to validate that conditional, right? Like, ‘no, no, no, trust me, pretty soon, theoretical physics is going to be mostly the domain of machines,’” Pines said. “And it’s not there yet, but it’s on its way.”

Still, while AI has claimed important solutions in fields like mathematics and computer science where it’s possible to express them in validated code, doing so in less abstracted disciplines like the life sciences or physics has proven more difficult. Last week, the startup Discovered Materials released a $1 million grand challenge for researchers using AI to understand problems like superconductivity and heat dissipation.

“At the end of the day, physics is different than math because it’s the real world … nature gets a vote in your models of reality,” Pines said. He said the startup is focused on understanding how to take computational results and validate them with experiments in the most efficient way possible.

“If it’s a true fact of nature, that’s a trick that you can exploit,” Pines said. “You could build a device out of it, right? The AI suggests an idea; it allows you to do something in the world you weren’t able to do before … and so each of those are kind of loops that PSI is building.”

items.title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google
items.summary: OpenAI is looking to make ChatGPT a more robust consumer discovery engine, and a host of new features seek to empower businesses to help it do that.
items.content:
In an effort to make ChatGPT an even better consumer discovery engine, OpenAI is launching a host of new features designed to help companies control how users interact with their businesses.

On Tuesday, the company rolled out a Business Hub that will serve as a place where companies can create business profiles that — in a feature that greatly resembles the kind of profiles that Google and other search engines already offer — allow enterprises to verify and update information about their products and services. The feature is currently in beta.

Eligible companies will also be able to create and launch a specialized business agent, which gives ChatGPT users the ability to ask questions about the business and its products.

“As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI,” the company said on Tuesday. “Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT.”

In a move that calls to mind Google Analytics , the Business Hub will also give users access to limited business insights. These insights will reveal how ChatGPT users interact with their products — including profile views, business mentions, website clicks, and other metrics.

Businesses will have to verify their profiles through a formal process, although the company did not share specifics of what that process would entail. Benji Shomair, OpenAI’s VP of Monetization, told journalists on Monday that there are “multiple verification methods that we use for different types of business in different markets.”

OpenAI previously tried to position ChatGPT as an e-commerce hub by which users could buy products directly. This effort — which used a commission fee system — was viewed as a potentially huge source of revenue and a way to make ChatGPT a more direct Amazon competitor. However, that project ultimately failed to take off and, in March, the company retired the effort , which had even included a “checkout cart” feature.

With the integration of business profiles and intelligence, ChatGPT seems to be attempting to become more like Google, which — since the advent of the internet — has been the place where web users go to understand the companies they want to shop at. It remains to be seen whether this initiative will bear better results than the one that sought to make ChatGPT a direct e-commerce hub.

items.content:
Nvidia's model GR00T 2 watches humans on video, then imagines itself as the robot

View the LinkedIn Profile of Maximilian Schreiner

To teach robots new tasks, humans usually have to laboriously teleoperate them during training. Nvidia's new AI model GR00T 2 is designed to cut that effort by transferring human movements from videos to robotic arms.

To train a robot for new tasks, engineers usually spend hours remotely controlling the machines. This so-called teleoperation is expensive, slow, and needs its own data for every robot model. In a new research report on GR00T 2 , Nvidia introduces a new AI foundation model designed to shorten this process.

Unlike previous approaches, including its predecessor GR00T 1, GR00T 2 doesn't translate camera images and language commands directly into motor movements. Nvidia says the software works as what the company calls a world-action model. It simultaneously calculates the next movement and a short video of the immediate future. The system predicts how the camera image should change when a robotic arm picks up an object, for example.

Unlike its predecessor, GR00T 2 is no longer a vision-language-action model. Nvidia calls it a world-action model (WAM) that also predicts what it will see in the future via diffusion. | Image: Nvidia

This video prediction should let the model transfer movement sequences between different robot form factors. Nvidia trained the system on a cluster with more than a thousand GB300 chips, including about 400,000 hours of video footage showing people performing various tasks while wearing head-mounted cameras.

To then teach a robot a new task, the researchers say it should be enough for a person to demonstrate the steps using data gloves, specialized hand grippers, or a finger exoskeleton. When these recordings are combined during training with general motion data from the target robot, the AI generates the robotic arm instead of the human arm in its video prediction and derives the matching control commands from that.

In lab tests, a robot with five-fingered hands was able to light a match, slice a banana, or toss packages onto a conveyor belt this way, without having been teleoperated for those specific tasks.

Success rates varied between 10 and 80 percent depending on the task. From a single video of a human hand movement, the system also learned to hammer nails by way of a computer simulation. For 50 selected tasks where the model already performed well after just a few examples, less than three minutes of conventional training was enough to raise the success rate from 40 to 95 percent.

A higher-level language model helps with errors but slows the robot down

For longer assembly work, Nvidia pairs the system with a higher-level AI language model like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. While GR00T 2 handles the gripping movements, the language model breaks the task into individual steps, color-codes grip points in the camera image, and launches helper routines when a part falls off.

When the researchers placed loose parts for toy models on a table in no particular order, the combined system assembled them in at least 97 percent of trials. Without the corrective language model and additional fine-tuning, the toy car assembly succeeded in only 23 out of 100 attempts. The team also trained precision tasks like plugging in network cables or chargers through repeated trial and error on the real device.

For bipedal robots, Nvidia developed the slimmed-down variant GR00T 2 Turbo, which processes fewer image details. It runs directly on the Jetson Thor onboard computer of a humanoid robot. In testing, the machine was able to scoop popcorn, clear tables, and wipe up liquids with a towel under its foot. That last task, though, succeeded in just under half of all attempts.

The research team identifies significant hurdles before the system is ready for reliable real-world use. The model doesn't yet process direct sensor data for touch and sometimes misses subtle errors…

items.content:
Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates released

Microsoft has released the Patch Tuesday Windows 11 KB513261 and KB5131087 cumulative updates for versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs and add new features.

Today's updates are mandatory as they contain the November 2026 Patch Tuesday security patches for hundreds of vulnerabilities discovered in previous months.

You can install today's update by going to  Start  >  Settings  >  Windows Update  and clicking on  'Check for Updates .'

You can also manually download and install the update from the  Microsoft Update Catalog .

This is the eleventh 'Patch Tuesday' release in 2026, and it's based on 24H2, which means 25H2 or 26H2 get the same update. There are no exclusive or special changes. You'll get the same fixes across the two versions of Windows 11.

What's new in the November 2026 Patch Tuesday update

With today's update, Microsoft is adding new customization options to Windows 11 and fixing minor issues with File Explorer.

Here's the full list of improvements and fixes:

New! This update introduces an updated context menu that is faster, simpler, and more customizable. The updated menu opens more quickly, reduces clutter, and gives you more control over the commands and app extensions that appear when you right-click.

You can now customize the context menu to better fit how you use Windows. Select Customize menu at the bottom of the context menu to open its Settings page.

Turn built-in Windows commands, such as Send to and Create shortcut , on or off.

Add commands such as Print to the context menu.

Choose which app extensions appear in the main menu or a submenu or hide the app extensions submenu.

Display Cut , Copy , Paste , Rename , Delete , and Share directly in the menu instead of as a row of icons.

Move Properties to the bottom of the context menu.

To personalize the context menu, right-click and select Customize menu , then choose the commands, app extensions, and layout you prefer. No action is required to use the default configuration. To see more options, hold down Shift and right-click on your desktop.

New! This update modernizes the AutoPlay dialog that appears when you connect devices such as a phone, camera, or removable drive to your PC. The updated experience supports dark mode, responds better to text scaling and display settings, and makes AutoPlay notifications available in notification center for easier access.

New! Key file information, such as name, location, and date, now appear in a consistent layout on the File Explorer search results page, making search results easier to scan.

New! Address bar now supports ~ , making it quicker to navigate directly to your user profile folder and subfolders (for example, ~\AppData ).

New! This update enables dark mode support in the Folder Options dialog in File Explorer.

New! This update introduces a refreshed Gaming Task View experience in XBOX mode, featuring a new navigation bar that provides quick access to Exit to Desktop and Power Options, making key system actions easier to access while gaming. 1

New! This update improves the Privacy & security page in Windows Settings by grouping related Camera, Microphone, and Location privacy controls and elevating usage information from linked pages onto the main page.

New! The Device Info card on the Settings Home page, first introduced in the March 2026 preview update KB5079391 , is expanding to additional markets. Available to users signed in with a Microsoft account, the card provides a quick view of key PC specifications and usage, with more detailed device information available under Settings > System > About . 1

This update makes some small visual refinements to the design of the temporary files section under Settings > System > Storage .

items.summary: Google is making Gemini 4 Carbon generally available after a two-week testing phase. The model ranks first in several benchmarks, in some cases ahead of Anthropic's new Fable 5.2, at less than half the per-task cost. Google is also previewing coordinated agent teams through the "
items.content:
Gemini 4 Carbon arrives just in time to feel like yesterday's news in the fastest model cycle yet

View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian

Google has made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available after a two-week testing phase for paying developers and business customers.

Carbon complements Gemini 4 Argon and is built for demanding tasks such as multi-step coding, debugging, and scientific research, though it consumes more tokens than Argon.

Google previewed the "/swarm" feature in Antigravity, which turns a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents that split up complex tasks in real time.

About two weeks ago, it looked as though Google would once again take the lead in AI models when it unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon. But the advertising and cloud giant took a bit too long to release it.

Now, Carbon is already starting to feel a little less fresh. Anthropic just unveiled its new top model, Fable 5.2 , which outperforms the new Gemini model in the Artificial Analysis test even at lower reasoning intensity. The model cycle is spinning particularly fast right now. Still, it's good to see that Carbon is now generally available after a two-week testing phase for selected security experts.

Google says Carbon complements the previously released Gemini 4 Argon rather than replacing it. Argon is still the better choice for most software engineering and knowledge work tasks, according to Google, while Carbon is built for tasks that push the limits of model intelligence. That's a bit surprising, since both models have the same token price, but Carbon scores higher on benchmarks. Ad

Google lists complex multi-step coding and debugging along with open-ended scientific research among Carbon's strengths. But the model uses more tokens than Argon to reason more deeply on complex debugging or open-ended research and to run longer verification loops. So in practice, the total bill is likely higher compared to Argon despite the same token price. Ad

In the Artificial Analysis test published two weeks ago, Carbon cost $7.76 per solved task, already calculated at the regular standard price of four dollars per million input tokens and 20 dollars per million output tokens. That makes Carbon cheaper than the older budget model Flash 3.8 while delivering better performance, which is no small feat. A Flash variant of Gemini 4 is likely to launch soon.

In the same test, Opus 5.5 Max comes in at $10.04, GPT-6 Astra Max at $6.25. Fable 5.2 at its maximum tier costs as much as $26.50. At the High tier, Fable 5.2 costs "only" about $9 per task but still sits two points ahead of Carbon in the overall index (62 vs. 60). Ad

Developers and business customers on paid tiers can access the model through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, in Android Studio, or through Gemini for Business. The introductory price stays at two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens.

Google introduces agent swarms that turn a single prompt into a coordinated AI agent team

Alongside the model launch, Google is previewing the "/swarm" feature in Google Antigravity, Google's counterpart to Claude Code. The new feature turns a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents whose work can be tracked in real time. Carbon takes on roles that need deep reasoning, such as architecture design, coordination, and auditing, while faster, lighter models run in parallel isolated workspaces and as adversarial verifiers. Ad

Google demonstrates the feature with a 3D game where users explore the Google campus in Mountain View as a pelican on a GBike, an interactive 3D reconstruction of the Eiffel Tower's construction based on historical photos, and a playable 18th-century fortepiano with seat-specific spatial acoustics. Ad

items.content:
구글 '제미나이'와 앤트로픽 '클로드'의 추격에도 오픈AI의 '챗GPT'가 글로벌 AI 챗봇 시장에서 압도적인 지위를 유지하고 있는 것으로 나타났다. 경쟁 서비스들이 빠르게 성장하는 가운데 챗GPT도 올해 상반기 하락했던 점유율을 최근 다시 회복하면서 주요 AI 챗봇 이용량의 81% 이상을 차지했다.

시장조사 업체 그래파이트(Graphite)는 9일(현지시간) 시밀러웹 데이터를 분석한 보고서 를 통해 챗GPT가 전 세계 주요 AI 챗봇 6종의 웹·앱 이용 세션 가운데 81.2%를 차지했다고 밝혔다.

조사 대상에는 챗GPT와 클로드, 제미나이, 그록, 퍼플렉시티, 딥시크가 포함됐다. 챗GPT를 제외하고 점유율 10%를 넘긴 서비스는 없었다.

챗GPT의 이용량도 다시 증가하고 있다. 2025년 상반기 급성장한 뒤 약 7개월간 정체됐지만, 올해 들어 증가세를 회복했다. 지난 9월에는 전년 동기 대비 24% 증가한 613억5000만건의 월간 이용 세션을 기록하며 사상 최고치를 경신했다. 최근 주간 사용자 수도 12억명에 달하는 것으로 알려졌다.

점유율은 올해 상반기 매달 평균 1%포인트씩 낮아졌으나, 7월부터 반등해 9월까지 약 0.8%포인트를 회복했다. 경쟁 서비스의 성장에도 챗GPT의 이용량이 다시 늘면서 시장 지위를 유지한 것이다.

2023년부터 2026년 9월까지 주요 AI 챗봇 6종의 전 세계 웹·앱 이용 세션 추이. 챗GPT가 압도적인 이용량을 유지하는 가운데 클로드와 제미나이 등 경쟁 서비스도 성장하고 있다. (사진=그래파이트·시밀러웹)

경쟁 서비스 가운데서는 클로드의 성장세가 가장 두드러졌다. 지난 1년간 이용 세션이 1901% 증가해 약 20배로 늘었으며, 9월에는 54억4000만건을 기록해 제미나이(37억2000만건)를 제치고 조사 대상 AI 챗봇 가운데 2위에 올랐다. 제미나이와 그록도 같은 기간 각각 182%, 123% 성장했다.

그러나 클로드와 제미나이 모두 상대적으로 작은 이용자 기반에서 출발해 빠르게 성장한 것으로, 챗GPT와의 절대적인 이용량 차이는 여전히 크다.

AI 서비스가 다른 웹사이트로 유입시키는 트래픽도 증가했다. 지난 1년간 AI 서비스에서 외부 웹사이트로 연결되는 전 세계 추천 트래픽은 92% 늘었다. 이 가운데 챗GPT가 전체의 60%를 차지해 AI 기반 정보 검색과 웹사이트 방문을 연결하는 주요 통로로 자리 잡았다.

구글 검색 시장에서도 AI 이용이 늘고 있다. 검색 결과에 AI 생성 답변을 제공하는 'AI 개요'는 지난 8월 미국 구글 검색의 64%에 노출됐다. 대화형 검색 서비스인 'AI 모드'도 빠르게 성장해 같은 달 미국에서 4억9100만건의 웹 방문을 기록했다.

이번 점유율 조사는 주요 AI 챗봇 6종의 이용 세션을 비교한 것으로, 구글 검색에 통합된 AI 모드 등은 포함하지 않았다. 따라서 챗GPT의 81.2%를 전체 생성 AI 이용 시장의 점유율로 해석할 수는 없다.

지역별로는 미국 외 시장의 비중이 컸다. 미국의 AI 서비스 트래픽 비중은 전 세계의 8.8%에 그쳤으며, 나머지 90% 이상은 다른 국가에서 발생했다. 주요 AI 서비스의 전 세계 월간 방문 수는 760억건으로, 전년보다 37% 증가했다.

items.content:
French software company Vates VMS has warned of a critical security vulnerability in Xen Orchestra that it said is being actively exploited in the wild.

The authentication bypass flaw, which does not yet have a CVE identifier, is tracked as VSA-2026-062 .

"REST cookie parsing turns authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D into {}," Vates VMS said in an alert. "REST authentication passes that object to the XO token provider without requiring a string."

"The token collection treats {} as an unfiltered lookup and returns its first token; the provider authenticates as that token's owner if it is unexpired. The authenticated /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens route then returns reusable login token IDs."

In other words, the vulnerability can allow an attacker to bypass authentication by sending a specially crafted cookie and perform arbitrary actions with "Admin" privileges, ultimately resulting in arbitrary code execution on managed pools and a full XCP-ng node takeover as root.

items.title: Adobe Patches 110 Vulnerabilities Across 9 Products
items.summary: Adobe has fixed vulnerabilities in AEM, Premiere, Photoshop, After Effects, Connect, Audition, Dimension, Content Credentials SDK, and Media Encoder. The post Adobe Patches 110 Vulnerabilities Across 9 Products appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
Adobe’s November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates fix roughly 110 vulnerabilities across nine products.

New patches are available for Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), Audition, After Effects, Connect, Content Credentials SDK, Dimension, Media Encoder, Photoshop, and Premiere.

Critical-severity issues have been patched in Adobe Connect and AEM, including six Connect flaws with a CVSS score of 10.

The critical flaws include SSRF, path traversal, incorrect authorization, CRLF injection, XXE, code injection, SQL injection, and XSS issues. They can be exploited for privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution.

A total of 38 vulnerabilities have been resolved in AEM and Connect, including high- and medium-severity issues whose exploitation can lead to privilege escalation, file system read, memory exposure, arbitrary code execution, and bypassing security features.

High-severity bugs have been fixed in After Effects, Media Encoder, Premiere, Dimension, Audition, and Photoshop.  Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

The Content Credentials Rust SDK (and the C2PA Tool) received patches for roughly a dozen low- and medium-severity issues.

Adobe says it’s not aware of attacks exploiting the newly patched vulnerabilities.

The Connect and AEM patches have a priority rating of 2; the rest are rated 3, which means they are unlikely to be exploited in the wild.

items.content:
Three distinct threat activity clusters with shared infrastructure and malware code similarities have been observed targeting telecommunications providers, government organizations, military entities, research institutions, and critical infrastructure across Latin America, Asia, and Europe over the past year.

Check Point Research is tracking the clusters under the names SilentDelivery , OceanGate , and DarkWire . Although initially assumed to be independent sets of attacks, each with its own backdoors and post-exploitation tooling, they have all been linked through a malware ecosystem called Sparrow.

The entity behind the Sparrow framework has been codenamed CopperDragon , and is assessed to be a digital quartermaster developing tools for China-nexus threat actors, including FamousSparrow , Earth Estries , Tropic Trooper , UAT-9244 , and UAT-8302 .

"Each cluster employed a different toolset and different initial access techniques, including compromising internet-facing infrastructure and highly selective watering hole attacks," Check Point said in a technical report published today. "The compromised websites that were used for watering hole attacks were of government, shipping, and IT and research sectors."

Attacks mounted by FamousSparrow are known for deploying backdoors like SparrowDoor (and its variants Crowdoor and TernDoor ), SparroWocky , and HemiGate . It's also assessed to share some degree of overlap with Salt Typhoon. However, the precise nature of the relationship remains unclear.

The cyber espionage ecosystem linked to CopperDragon is driven by three prominent clusters -

The SilentDelivery chain begins with the attacker injecting heavily obfuscated JavaScript into legitimate websites frequented by their intended targets. Visitors to the sites are greeted by a Google Chrome SSL certificate warning that instructs users to install a "Certificate Fix" utility to restore access.

The so-called utility, once deployed, delivers either SquadC or a SparrowDoor variant. All the compromised websites have been found to be related to government, shipping, IT, and research sectors in the Czech Republic, Germany, France, Taiwan, Nepal, Hong Kong, and Indonesia.

According to a report published by Positive Technologies in August 2026, there are indications that the campaign has also targeted entities in Egypt and the Philippines using this method.

"The JavaScript injected into the compromised websites is heavily obfuscated using jsjiami, a publicly available JavaScript obfuscation service," Check Point said. "It first checks whether the user is running Windows and, in some cases, verifies that the website’s domain matches the intended compromised domain."

The script then repeatedly sends status-check requests to a command-and-control (C2) server to fingerprint the user based on IP and geolocation, and ultimately decide whether to continue the attack and serve the fake warning.

Written in C/C++, SquadC is a Windows backdoor that enables initial foothold over the infected host. It establishes persistence by means of a Windows Registry Run key that masquerades as a Windows update assistant. Further analysis has uncovered that the malware is also distributed via phishing emails targeting Indonesian organizations.

The phishing email comes with a Windows Shortcut (LNK) disguised as a PDF document, which, when opened, abuses the legitimate "ftp.exe" binary to run a batch script that's responsible for displaying an empty file as a decoy, while launching SquadC via DLL sideloading.

items.content:
'운영하고 있는 시스템에 취약점이 발견되었을 경우에, 즉시 패치를 적용하지 않은 것은 시스템 운영자의 책임 방기이며 직무유기이다. 따라서 앞으로는 패치를 적용하지 않은 것이 드러날 경우에 담당자·CEO 문책과 매출 대비 % 과징금 부과 등 엄중한 책임을 묻겠다'

요즘 자주 듣게 되는 이야기이다. 그런데 세상 모든 일이 그러하듯 현장의 상황은 생각보다 무척 복잡하다.

무엇보다 '패치 적용'은 전산장애를 일으킬 수 있다. '서버 OS를 업그레이드했더니 애플리케이션이 돌아가지 않는다'라는 사례가 있는 것처럼 소프트웨어 모듈은 서로 간에 종속성이 많아서, 하나가 변경되었을 때 다른 쪽이 어떤 영향을 받게 될지는 사전에 파악하기가 쉽지 않다. 퍼블릭 클라우드 인프라에서 운영되는 시스템 또한 정도의 차이가 있을 수 있지만 이러한 영향에서 자유로울 수 없다.

금융, 통신 기관의 경우, 전산 장애가 발생한다면 손해액은 시간당 수십억 원이 될 수도 있다. 회사의 평판 또한 심각한 타격을 받는다. 또한 금융기관은 심각한 전산장애 발생 시 담당자 및 임원, 그리고 CEO에게까지 징계가 내려온다.

이에 따라서 패치는 물론이고 시스템 업그레이드 또한 매우 신중하게 진행될 수밖에 없다. 생산 공장 같은 경우에는 시스템이 한 번 돌아가기 시작하면 변경하기가 쉽지 않고 10년 동안 그대로 쓰는 경우가 적지 않다. 그렇기 때문에 패치 적용보다는 네트워크 폐쇄로 대응한다.

패치 적용 시 장애 리스크를 관리하기 위해서는 시스템 이중화 투자가 필요하다. 먼저 하나의 시스템에 패치를 적용한 후에 문제가 없으면 다른 곳에 적용한다. 패치 적용 후 장애가 발생하면 원복하고, 원복이 바로 되지 않더라도 남아 있는 시스템에서 정상적인 서비스를 수행할 수 있다.

인프라가 낙후된 경우에는 일부 솔루션과 장비가 서비스 지원 기간이 만료되어서(End of Service) 패치 적용이 불가능한 경우도 있다. 서버 전수 검사를 진행했을 때 전체의 30% 정도가 지원 만료 상태인 것은 결코 특수한 상황이 아니다. 이 경우 패치 적용을 위해서 시스템을 최신 형상으로 업그레이드하는 사전 작업을 수행해야 한다. 이처럼 패치는 적지 않은 금전적인 투자가 반드시 수반되어야 한다.

모든 취약점에 대해서 패치를 반드시 신속하게 적용해야만 하는 것은 아니다. 외부에 오픈된 시스템이 아니라 내부의 폐쇄망에서 운영되는 시스템의 취약점은 공격받을 수 있는 가능성이 매우 낮기 때문에 패치 적용까지 상당 기간의 시간적 여유를 가지고 준비할 수 있다. 중요 서버는 다른 네트워크와 접점을 최소화하고, 접근할 수 있는 단말을 한정한다. 해당 단말 또한 네트워크를 물리적으로 단절하는 것으로 대처하기도 한다. 위에서 언급한 것처럼 생산 공장은 자체 IT 인력도 제한적이기 때문에 네트워크 자체를 폐쇄하는 것으로 대응하는 경우가 많다.

솔루션 개발업체는 자사 솔루션의 취약점이 발견됐을 때 패치를 신속하게 릴리스하는 역할을 수행한다. 릴리스된 패치를 사이트에 적용하는 것은 고객사가 자신의 감독하에 고객이 스스로 적용하거나 해당 기관 IT 운영업체가 수행한다. 이는 전 세계 소프트웨어 업체의 표준 관행이다.

그러나 한국에서는 솔루션 개발사에게 사이트에 패치를 적용하는 작업까지 무상으로 요청하는 경우가 적지 않다. 패치 적용은 사전 준비, 적용, 모니터링의 세 단계로 구성되어서, 시스템 환경에 따라 짧게는 이틀에서 길게는 일주일까지 소요될 수 있다. 1,000개의 사이트에 솔루션을 납품한 회사의 경우 모든 고객 사이트에 직접 패치를 적용한다면 인력 비용만 몇 십억 원이 넘게 발생할 수 있다.

이처럼 국내 솔루션 개발사 입장에서 자사 솔루션의 취약점을 적극적으로 공개하기 어려운 이유는 취약점 공개 이후 '패치 적용' 작업을 부담해야 하기 때문이다. 향후에는 최소한 '실비 보전'을 해주는 것으로 관행이 점차 바뀔 것으로 기대한다.

이처럼 ‘패치 적용’은 단순히 담당자의 게으름이나 책임 방기의 문제가 아니다. 서비스 안정성에 대한 문제이고, 전산장애 시 책임에 대한 문제이며, 무엇보다도 투자 비용의 문제이다. 요즘과 같은 AI로 인한 '대'취약점 폭발 시대에, IT 담당자와 보안 담당자의 고민은 심각해질 수밖에 없다. 문제의 복잡성을 이해하고, 우선순위에 따라서 어떻게 해결해 나갈지 하나하나 신중하게 의사결정을 하며 풀어나가야 할 문제이다.

희망적인 점은 앞으로는 패치를 적용하더라도 장애를 최소화할 수 있도록 인프라와 솔루션 개발이 가속화되고 있다는 것이다. 솔루션 자체를 도커 기반으로 설계하는 것이 그 하나의 예이다. 신규 솔루션 도입은 이러한 방식으로 해결할 수 있다 하더라도 기존 레거시 시스템에 대한 패치 관리는 여전히 상당 기간 끌고 가야 할 숙제이다.

items.summary: SBOM pioneer Allan Friedman joined the SecurityWeek Podcast to discuss why knowing what is inside software is only the beginning, how AI is complicating software supply chain visibility, and what organizations should be doing with SBOM data once they have it. The post Software Tr
items.content:
Modern software is built on layers of dependencies, open source components, third party libraries and increasingly, artificial intelligence models and external data sources. For security teams, understanding exactly what is running inside an application has become less of a compliance exercise and more of an operational necessity.

That is the foundation behind the Software Bill of Materials, or SBOM.

In a recent episode of the SecurityWeek Podcast , host Brian “SchleiF” Schleifer sat down with cybersecurity policy expert Allan Friedman for a wide-ranging discussion about the origins of SBOM, how organizations should actually use the data, the emergence of AI BOMs, vulnerability management, VEX, and where software transparency may be heading next.

Friedman, who helped drive early government and industry work around SBOM, offered perhaps the simplest explanation for why the concept matters.

“Software isn’t written, it’s assembled,” Friedman said. “What’s it assembled out of? More software.”

In practical terms, an SBOM provides a structured representation of the components and dependencies that allow software to function. But Friedman emphasized throughout the conversation that producing an SBOM is not the end goal. The real value comes from what organizations, and their suppliers can do with the information. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

SBOM Is About Response, Not Just Inventory

Much of the early SBOM conversation focused on whether vendors could generate the documents and whether customers should require them.

The more important question today may be: What happens after you receive one?

Friedman argues that one of the first indicators of software supply chain maturity is simply knowing that a supplier can generate an accurate SBOM.

That capability becomes critical when organizations face the next Log4j style vulnerability, compromise of a major software package, malicious update, or other widespread supply chain event.

A supplier that understands the components within its products can determine its exposure far more quickly than one forced to reconstruct dependencies during an incident. For customers, the same visibility can dramatically shorten response time.

Instead of spending days or weeks contacting vendors and attempting to determine which systems contain a vulnerable component, security teams can analyze their software inventory and dependencies directly.

The objective, however, should ultimately be deeper integration.

Friedman said SBOM information needs to become another source of enterprise security data, feeding vulnerability management, asset management, procurement and continuous risk management processes rather than existing as a static document stored somewhere for future reference.

That distinction matters because attackers are not limited to vulnerabilities associated with the name of the software vendor.

A smaller vendor’s application may contain an outdated framework, library or open source component with a known weakness. Without component level visibility, an organization may never associate that vulnerability with the commercial product deployed in its environment.

Not Every Vulnerability Creates the Same Risk

More visibility can also create another problem: more alerts.

Finding that a vulnerable component exists inside an application does not necessarily mean the vulnerability is exploitable within that specific implementation.

Friedman highlighted the Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange, or VEX, as an important companion to SBOM. VEX provides a machine processable method for communicating whether a vulnerability actually affects a product.

items.title: Google Widens Gemini 4 Carbon Access After AI Agents Verify Signal Code
items.summary: Google opened Carbon to paying developers and businesses as DeepMind used agents built on it to prove libsignal security guarantees. The post Google Widens Gemini 4 Carbon Access After AI Agents Verify Signal Code appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
Google on Tuesday expanded access to Gemini 4 Carbon and said agents built on the model helped formally verify core security guarantees in the code behind the Signal protocol.

Paying developers and businesses can now use Carbon via the Gemini API and Gemini for business, and Google AI Ultra subscribers are getting access. Introductory rates of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens apply until November 30, then double.

Until now, only select cyber defenders in Google’s Fairwind Program could use Carbon. They still need Fairwind membership for Carbon for cyber, which Google says tops key benchmarks for discovering, exploiting and fixing vulnerabilities.

According to Google, Wiz used Carbon for cyber to find zero-days at two major SaaS providers within two hours. Google’s Cloud Vulnerability Research (CVR) team used the model to confirm that two bugs in a popular open source project were exploitable, with severity comparable to PHP2Shell , a pair of PHP flaws that attackers have already exploited.

“By using Carbon to build a proof of concept, CVR helped maintainers re-classify the bug as critical and swiftly issue a patch,” Google said .

Separately, Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code , which pairs human experts with AI agents to formally verify software, mathematically demonstrating that it meets defined requirements. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

The team applied it to libsignal, the Signal protocol’s reference implementation. Versions of the protocol also run in WhatsApp and Google Messages.

Humans worked with agents running on Carbon and Claude Opus 5.5 to write the specifications defining what had to be proven. Carbon-based agents then generated all of the roughly 6.5 million lines of Lean proofs, with Lean rejecting any invalid ones.

The proven guarantees, including forward secrecy, post-compromise security, and authentication, hold for the compiled machine code, while most protocol verification examines only the design.

Five researchers did the proof work in four weeks, something Google says has traditionally taken specialists years.

To show the method catches real flaws, the team reinserted two old, already-patched libsignal bugs and proved that those builds break the security guarantees.

The results cover Google’s own build of the code, run through a small command-line wrapper, and “not Signal’s own applications.” Side channels were also excluded from parts of the analysis.

“The results suggest that AI can make formal verification, historically too expensive for most software, practical for real-world systems,” the researchers wrote .

“As AI-driven security threats grow, rigorously verifying the Signal protocol implementation gives us even greater confidence in our code’s privacy guarantees,” said Signal CTO Ehren Kret.

Google is publicly releasing the specifications and proofs.

items.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks that could grant administrator privileges and allow takeover of XCP-ng virtualization hosts. [...]
items.content:
Critical Xen Orchestra auth bypass flaw exploited to hijack VM servers

A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks that could grant administrator privileges and allow takeover of XCP-ng virtualization hosts.

Xen Orchestra is a web-based management platform developed by French software company Vates, used to manage XCP-ng virtualization environments, including virtual machines, hosts, and pools.

The vulnerability, tracked as VSA-2026-062, affects Xen Orchestra and the Xen Orchestra Appliance (XOA) and allows remote attackers with network access to the management interface to bypass authentication using a specially crafted cookie. A CVE identifier and CVSS score have not been assigned yet.

According to a Vates security advisory , the flaw stems from how Xen Orchestra processes authentication tokens sent through REST API requests.

The flaw stems from how Xen Orchestra processes authentication cookies.

By sending a specially crafted cookie ( authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D ) containing an empty JSON object ( {} ), attackers can trick the platform into retrieving an existing authentication token and logging them in as its owner, without requiring actual credentials.

Once authenticated, attackers can retrieve "reusable login token IDs" through the /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens  REST API endpoint, which can be used for further access.

"An adversary can bypass authentication and perform actions with 'Admin' privilege. Xen Orchestra compromise can lead to arbitrary code execution on managed pools and a full XCP-ng node takeover as root ," warns Vates .

The company has released Xen Orchestra 6.9.1 (stable) and 6.10.0 (latest), including patched xo-server packages 5.211.2 and 5.213.1 to fix these security vulnerabilities.

Administrators should install the update immediately, and if not possible, restrict Xen Orchestra access to dedicated management networks and block known malicious IP addresses.

Security researchers Filip Magic and Christoffer Olsen of TDC NET Security discovered the vulnerability.

Vates confirmed that the vulnerability is being actively exploited and shared the following indicators of compromise (IOCs) to help administrators identify attacks:

Attacker's infrastructure: Connections to  91.211.251.112:8001 or ustar3rqxgnskzgnwkgpofgtvxevm6cx3lxdbwt4mndtveqyaohid.onion:3333 .

Suspicious authentication cookies: HTTP requests containing authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D or authenticationToken=j:{} .

Modified VM configurations: Virtual machines configured with the hvm_serial: file parameter.

Unusual files: /etc/cron.d/zz-ustar , /etc/cron.d/zz-ustar2 , /.ustar5 , and /.ustar6 .

Administrators can also run the following commands on XCP-ng hosts to check for unusual VM configurations, virtual machines configured to use a file for its serial port, and malicious files:

xe vm-list params=name-label,platform | grep -B1 'hvm_serial: file'

zgrep -- '-serial file:' /var/log/xensource.log*

ls -la /etc/ld.so.preload /.ustar* /etc/cron.d/zz-ustar*

However, Vates warns that exploitation will not generate any identifiers in logs, such as the use of specially crafted cookies, and instead must be detected through HTTP monitoring.

The company also says these IOCs are only associated with this known attack campaign and may differ for other threat actors.

Companies that believe they are compromised should rotate passwords and secrets used by their virtualization environments.

items.summary: Fireworks said the incident affected a “limited number of customer accounts” — all of whom were notified of the attack.
items.content:
Image: Fireworks AI AI company Fireworks says hackers stole data, billing info during October breaches

AI infrastructure company Fireworks said cybercriminals stole billing information and AI-specific data during two breaches last month.

Fireworks published an updated notice on Monday saying it hired Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 to investigate a data breach it initially discovered on October 6 . The San Mateo-based company was founded in 2022 and has more than 10,000 customers, offering an array of AI systems and tools to companies.

Investigators found that a well-known, financially motivated cybercriminal group launched the attack and stole account and billing information as well as secrets — confidential digital pieces of information that grant access to human users or apps and allow them to communicate or perform actions. Fireworks said the incident affected a “limited number of customer accounts” — all of whom were notified of the attack.

Monday’s alert from Fireworks also notes that the company experienced another incident on October 23 where a third-party cloud provider that hosted their R&D machines was attacked by cybercriminals.

“On October 24, the unauthorized third party used [the provider] to reach Fireworks development machines and then run an unauthorized workload that led to additional customer data impact,” the company said.

The hackers gained access to internal Fireworks data, billing information, invoices and payment history as well as datasets and other AI-related data.

The customers that were impacted have been notified. Fireworks is working with Palo Alto Networks on hardening its security posture and revoking compromised credentials.

Digital workspace company Notion released its own notice that some of its customers were impacted by the Fireworks breaches. The company said it was notified of the incident on November 2 and disconnected its systems from Fireworks, deleting all data in the Fireworks system.

“On November 6, Fireworks notified us that malicious actors may have accessed potential customer data. Our team immediately began another internal investigation,” the company said.

“We used Fireworks for classification jobs to help customers understand their own AI usage through a feature in Notion called Insights, and we used them as a general inference provider to serve open-weight models inside our product. The Insights feature has been disabled as we investigate this incident, and we are no longer serving open-weight models through Fireworks.”

Fireworks said its breaches are part of a larger string of attacks recently spotlighted by incident responders at Google. Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant published a blog last week about a tactic known as "LLMJacking” where hackers hijack an enterprise’s access to large language models.

Mandiant said it has responded to multiple LLMJacking incidents in 2026 spanning a variety of cloud and LLM providers while impacting “organizations in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific across the financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors.”

“Unlike the gradual resource consumption associated with cryptojacking, LLMJacking can generate large spikes in fraudulent cloud charges in a matter of hours,” the researchers explained.

“Across individual incidents, we observed fraudulent charges associated with resource consumption exceeding $100,000 in a single day, with cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1 million before access was revoked.”

GTIG said it has identified a "diverse set of financially motivated threat clusters operating out of multiple regions globally" that are responsible for the attacks.

The groups are also maturing — with some focusing on initial access before handing off to other groups that monetize and resell the unauthorized access to large language models.

items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of an attack that exploited two now-patched vulnerabilities in AhsayCBS to deliver a Python-based implant. The activity, observed by Huntress in early October 2026, involves the exploitation of a chain comprising CVE-2026-105133 an
items.content:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of an attack that exploited two now-patched vulnerabilities in AhsayCBS to deliver a Python-based implant.

The activity, observed by Huntress in early October 2026, involves the exploitation of a chain comprising CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands on affected systems. Patches for the two vulnerabilities were released by Ahsay Backup in mid-October 2026.

The two vulnerabilities are assessed to have been weaponized as zero-days, with the managed security platform first observing threat actors employing a smash-and-grab approach to deploy web shells and XMRig cryptocurrency miners on compromised systems.

"However, this incident reflects a much larger intrusion with more patience; the operator planted shells in several places, ran two different miners, staged tunneling tools, and installed a custom implant, all on servers whose job is to hold backups," Huntress researcher Jonathan Semon said.

Specifically, the unknown threat actor is said to have left five families of Jakarta Server Pages (JSP, formerly JavaServer Pages) web shells -

"[AhsayCBS.jsp's] disguise as an internal image preview service even extended down to a comment block describing a watermark endpoint," Huntress explained. "The web shell used only JSP implicit objects and fully qualified class names, meaning it would compile on any servlet container and on Java Development Kit (JDK) 6 and later."

The attack, besides deploying an XMRig miner masquerading as Microsoft Edge, has been found to deliver a second XMRig miner ("kvm-agent.exe") that restarts every minute through a SYSTEM scheduled task, while using a different wallet and mining pool.

The most notable aspect of the intrusion revolves around the Python backdoor ("main.py"), which is designed to run only on the host it's staged on and prevent it from executing within a sandbox or an analyst's machine.

It achieves this by computing the SHA-256 cryptographic hash of the host's MachineGuid and looks for a marker file with the same name in the same directory housing the Python implant, and then runs an embedded x64 DLL in memory that contacts a command-and-control (C2) server ("creepexplosiondarknight[.]com").

In an attempt to fly under the radar, the attack chain also configures Microsoft Defender exclusions, while serving tunneling tools (GOST and Chisel) and legitimate remote access software (AnyDesk, Atera, and Splashtop) to establish persistent access.

Evidence indicates that the threat actor may have targeted servers holding or managing backups.

"On a related Veeam server in the same environment, we also saw a command consistent with NetExec's Veeam credential-theft module: a PowerShell script, apparently launched remotely through WMI, that queried the VeeamBackup PostgreSQL database for stored credentials and decrypted them with DPAPI," Semon said.

"Backup software holds credentials for hypervisors, repositories and domain accounts. We cannot say how many of those credentials were retrieved, but the pairing of an Ahsay foothold with a Veeam credential query suggested the operator was interested in backup infrastructure on purpose, not by accident."

items.title: Binance warns of iOS flaw that could leak crypto wallet secrets
items.summary: Binance is warning about a vulnerability in Apple's iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 that could allow third-party apps to read private files stored by other apps, including cryptocurrency seed phrases, secret keys, and login credentials. [...]
items.content:
Binance warns of iOS flaw that could leak crypto wallet secrets

Binance is warning about a vulnerability in Apple’s iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 that could allow third-party apps to read private files stored by other apps, including cryptocurrency seed phrases, secret keys, and login credentials.

The crypto exchange clarifies that the issue is at the iOS level and does not impact only the Binance app.

“A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem,” Binance says .

At this time, no cryptocurrency losses have been confirmed, but Binance urges users to install the update immediately as a precaution.

The company recommends that users delete any unnecessary and untrusted apps and apply the latest versions for iOS and other apps.

Where compromise is suspected, Binance advises users to transfer funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions.

“worse_query” is a publicly disclosed iOS sandbox escape technique that allows an application to cross security boundaries and access the storage of other applications.

Yesterday, a proof-of-concept exploit has been published that uses a tool called WQ Files to perform attacks relying on the technique. Specifically, WQ Files uses “worse_query” to browse, export, edit, and delete other apps’ data without requiring a jailbreak.

The tool must be installed on an iPhone for the attack to work, but an attacker could distribute it through untrusted sources as a sideloaded app, bypassing Apple's App Store.

WQ Files has been confirmed to work on iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2, the same versions that Binance warned about.

Apple on November 9 released iOS security updates (iOS 27.2.1, 26.7.3, and 18.7.12) that address nine flaws. One of the fixed vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-113963, could allow an app to access sensitive user data.

It is unclear if this is the same security issue Binance is warning of, though.

The CVE-2026-113963 problem was reported by László Várady flaw, who found that the access occurred through App Intents, not App Group containers.

BleepingComputer has contacted Apple for clarifications and a request for comment, and we will add an update once we receive more details.

items.summary: The threat actor known as Blind Eagle has resurfaced with a new campaign targeting organizations in Latin America through judicial and administrative-themed phishing lures to deliver a remote access trojan (RAT) that shares its lineage with AsyncRAT and DCRat. "The campaign uses
items.content:
The threat actor known as Blind Eagle has resurfaced with a new campaign targeting organizations in Latin America through judicial and administrative-themed phishing lures to deliver a remote access trojan (RAT) that shares its lineage with AsyncRAT and DCRat.

"The campaign uses Portuguese and Spanish lures that resemble court notifications, fiscalía notices, tutela proceedings , and administrative documents," Zenox said in a report shared with The Hacker News.

Assessed to be a Spanish-speaking group and active since 2018, Blind Eagle (aka APT-C-36) has a track record of using spear-phishing lures to distribute commodity RATs like AsyncRAT, BitRAT, Lime RAT, NjRAT, Quasar RAT, and Remcos RAT.

Attack chains begin with phishing emails targeting individuals who handle cases, contracts, judicial, or institutional service requests to trick them into opening a malware-laced attachment.

One email containing a Colombian judicial-themed XHTML file has been identified as a weaponized Scalable Vector Graphics ( SVG ) image that renders a bogus web page impersonating Colombia's Fiscalía General de la Nación, also referred to as the Office of the Attorney General.

The web page, for its part, employs a technique known as HTML smuggling to assemble the next-stage ZIP archive payload locally in the web browser using ZipCrypto, thereby circumventing email security controls.

Present within the ZIP archive is a JavaScript dropper that masquerades as Network Configuration Auditor version 2.7.298. The JavaScript code conducts environment reconnaissance, and collects details such as system version, network profile, installation date, memory size, computer name, environment variables, and directories localized in Portuguese and Spanish.

Upon execution, it launches a Visual Basic Script that performs Windows Antimalware Scan Interface ( AMSI ) and Event Tracing for Windows ( ETW ) bypass, while displaying a fake criminal-citation page as a distraction mechanism.

In parallel, the malware also takes steps to delete the original XHTML artifact, clears Mark of the Web (MotW) metadata, and sets up persistence on the host under the Windows Startup folder so that it's automatically executed on system startup.

The attack culminates with the use of PowerShell to decode and launch the final RAT payload in memory. The trojan is an AsyncRAT fork with DCRat lineage based on code structure, configuration, build characteristics, and observed behavior.

"The targeting of judicial, fiscal, administrative and educational organizations gives the operation access to highly sensitive legal, financial and institutional information," Zenox said.

"Combined with the Portuguese and Spanish lures, Brazilian infrastructure, operational timezone and regional victimology, these elements establish the campaign as an APT-C-36 operation conducted through a Brazilian operational cluster."

Zenox told The Hacker News that it could not confirm whether any of these attacks had succeeded against real-world targets. However, during the campaign period between late October and early November 2026, it observed a large-scale wave of targeted phishing involving nearly 3,300 malicious emails.

While not all of these messages targeted organizations in Colombia, the country continues to remain a priority target for Blind Eagle for a combination of reasons.

"The repeated targeting of Colombia likely reflects multiple factors, with one of the main enabling factors being the structural vulnerabilities and uneven security maturity across parts of the country's critical, public, financial, and private-sector infrastructure," Zenox security researcher Gabriel Alves said.

"These conditions may increase the likelihood of successful compromises and offer greater opportunities to monetize access, steal sensitive data or funds, or reuse compromised credentials against critical systems.
